consensus_summary: Primary consensus identifies 'poor, meek, needy' as the anawim: the spiritually humble and lowly who recognize total dependence on God (not self, status, or power), receive divine favor/deliverance, and inherit the kingdom/earth (esp. via Beatitudes and OT Psalms/prophets); material poverty and remnant readings are common overlapping alternatives.
book_summary: The bowed-humble before God (one Hebrew word-family for poor/meek, with needy as companion), empty-handed toward Him and thus able to receive: the gospel’s hearers and heirs of the kingdom.
consensus_core_identification: anawim / spiritually humble dependents on God who inherit the kingdom
book_core_identification: bowed-humble before God, empty-handed receivers who hear the gospel and inherit the kingdom
rationale: Minimum cores are identical: both center on the humble/dependent posture before God (anawim tradition) that makes one receptive to the gospel and an heir of the kingdom. Book wording ('bowed-humble,' 'empty-handed,' Hebrew family note) is merely more concise and does not alter referent, conditions, or cases; shared primary scriptures confirm equivalence rather than refinement or replacement.
strongest_objection: Book’s exclusive spiritual focus might be said to underplay the common material-poverty alternative that some consensus responses treat as co-primary, but this does not change the shared core referent.
